note: Canonical evidence ledger. Markdown view is derived by tooling (P2). One record per source, never grouped.

records.study_design: production deployment evaluation comparing V0 and V1 architectures
records.population: production OpenHands deployments across models and benchmarks
records.finding: Moving the agent loop to event-sourced conversations with composable runtime services substantially reduced system-attributable failures over the prior architecture at negligible overhead.
records.applicability_limits: Authors evaluate their own system, though with production-scale data; vendor benchmark figures must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.source: Tests as Prompt / WebApp1K TDD benchmark
records.study_design: benchmark evaluation
records.population: 1,000 synthetic single-file web-app challenges
records.finding: When tests are the prompt, TDD success is governed by instruction-following and in-context learning rather than raw coding skill, so the active test set must stay small and salient to avoid instruction loss.
records.applicability_limits: WebApp1K is synthetic and single-file scale; it does not measure repository-level work or regression risk, and results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.study_design: benchmark evaluation with ablations
records.population: SWE-bench Verified Python repos
records.finding: Targeted test-impact analysis cut regressions on SWE-bench Verified from 6.08% to 1.82%, while generic TDD instructions without contextual data made regressions worse at 9.94%, so surfacing context beats prescribing procedure.
records.applicability_limits: Evaluated on SWE-bench Verified Python repos and dependent on existing test suites being meaningful; benchmark results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.
records.counter_evidence: Its own ablation shows procedural TDD mandates without context worsen regressions, countering any blanket TDD-instruction doctrine.

records.source: TDFlow: Agentic Workflows for Test-Driven Development (EACL 2026)
records.study_design: benchmark evaluation (800 runs)
records.population: SWE-bench Verified tasks with human-written tests supplied
records.finding: With human-written tests supplied, a narrowly engineered test-driven workflow reaches 94.3% on SWE-bench Verified with only 7 test-hacking cases in 800 runs, so resolving given tests is near-solved and accurate test generation is the remaining bottleneck.
records.applicability_limits: Assumes tests are supplied; sub-agent separation is scoped around the test oracle, not planning; SWE-bench Verified results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.
records.counter_evidence: arXiv 2602.07900 finds agent-written test volume does not change outcomes; TDFlow's gains rely on supplied human tests, not agent-generated ones.

records.source: TDDev: Multi-Agent TDD for Full-Stack Web Apps
records.study_design: controlled comparison against no-TDD baselines
records.population: full-stack web application generation tasks
records.finding: Converting requirements to structured acceptance tests before coding improved web-app generation quality by 34 to 48 percentage points, but only when the TDD enforcement protocol matched the model's building style; mismatches negated gains and inflated tokens up to 25x.
records.applicability_limits: Web-application domain only, measured against no-TDD baselines rather than lighter-weight verification alternatives; results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.
records.counter_evidence: arXiv 2602.07900 finds raising agent test volume by prompt does not improve outcomes, and arXiv 2607.05139 shows coupled test generation halves fault detection.

records.source: Rethinking the Value of Agent-Generated Tests
records.study_design: trajectory analysis with prompt interventions
records.population: SWE-bench Verified runs
records.finding: Test-writing frequency is similar in resolved and unresolved runs, agent tests are mostly observational prints rather than assertions, and prompt interventions on test volume do not significantly change outcomes, so mandating more agent-written tests reshapes cost, not quality.
records.applicability_limits: Trajectory analysis plus prompt interventions, not controlled ablations on identical patches; SWE-bench Verified only; does not directly test test-first versus test-after; results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.
records.counter_evidence: TDAD (arXiv 2603.17973) and TDFlow (EACL 2026) show test-driven signals help when the oracle is independent or human-written.

records.source: On the Risk of Coding Before Testing
records.study_design: controlled comparison of test-generation orderings
records.population: task-level programming problems and agentic workflows
records.finding: Generating tests after faulty code roughly halves fault detection versus generating them independently (14% vs 25%) because implementation and tests become mutually consistent and conceal defects; independence of the test from the implementation context is the load-bearing property, not test-first timing.
records.applicability_limits: Task-level programming problems; the authors note coupled-generation pipelines in other studies may already be contaminated by this effect; results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.study_design: benchmark comparison of a fixed pipeline against autonomous agents
records.population: SWE-bench issue-fixing tasks
records.finding: A simple fixed localise-repair-validate pipeline matched or beat contemporary autonomous agents at far lower cost (32.0% at $0.70 in its era), showing structured decomposition was largely a workaround for weak models.
records.applicability_limits: Advantage measured against 2024-era agents on SWE-bench; results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.
records.counter_evidence: Current SWE-bench Pro leaders are long-horizon agentic systems, which is contrary evidence against fixed pipelines for strong models.

records.source: Coverage and Mutation Score Correlation for LLM Tests (ISSTA 2026)
records.study_design: replicability study
records.population: LLM-generated test suites
records.finding: Coverage and mutation scores of LLM-generated suites are informative in regression-style settings where the code is assumed correct but unreliable when the code under test may already be buggy, so they cannot substitute for independent oracles.
records.applicability_limits: Replication diverges from classic human-test findings and the authors caution against generalising across all LLM test-generation workflows; results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.source: METR RCT on AI tools and experienced OSS developers
records.study_design: randomised controlled trial
records.population: 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 tasks, mature repos with high tacit knowledge
records.finding: In a randomised trial, experienced developers were 19% slower with early-2025 AI tools while believing they were 20% faster, so throughput claims need measurement because self-report inverts the sign.
records.applicability_limits: Early-2025 tooling on mature repos with high tacit knowledge; may not generalise to 2026 models, greenfield work or agent-heavy workflows; contrary evidence to the strong-model assumption, not proof agents stay slow.

records.finding: Define the machine-readable contract once in a typed schema, version it by date so consumers pin behaviour to a concrete revision, and make optional behaviour opt-in via capability negotiation rather than universal mandate.
records.applicability_limits: MCP governs tool and data connectivity, not development process; its ceremony lessons transfer only by analogy.

records.version_or_commit: protocol v1.0.0, negotiated via A2A-Version header; repo ~598 commits
records.finding: Model agent work as stateful Tasks with a small explicit state machine, and separate Tasks (state) from Messages (ephemeral communication) from Artifacts (durable outputs), with progress observed per declared capability.
records.applicability_limits: A2A treats agents as opaque and says nothing about internal planning or verification; its client-server semantics need adaptation for a single-repo estate.

records.version_or_commit: unknown release; Schema URL still 'TODO'; 600+ commits; conventions recently split from open-telemetry/semantic-conventions (which was at ~v1.59.0)
records.finding: Instrument agent work with standard span types and shared gen_ai attributes plus token-usage metrics so throughput and quality are measurable with off-the-shelf tooling rather than hand-written session logs.
records.applicability_limits: The gen_ai conventions are development-status, not stable; attribute names may change, so anything built on them must tolerate renames.

records.finding: A formal three-level loading contract (metadata at startup, full body on activation, resources on demand) with hard size limits keeps skill cost near zero until needed.
records.applicability_limits: Young de facto standard driven mainly by Anthropic; cross-agent portability of fields like allowed-tools is explicitly variable.

records.source: Playwright test retries and flake classification
records.version_or_commit: docs current as of Playwright v1.62 era; page undated
records.finding: Classify outcomes as passed, flaky and failed as first-class states and report flakes explicitly instead of hiding them behind green builds, preferring isolation over retries as the fix.
records.applicability_limits: Retry-on-failure can mask genuine race conditions; the doc offers the mechanism but no quantified flake-budget policy.

records.version_or_commit: feature introduced v1.46; notes current to v1.62
records.finding: Affected-test selection is a built-in git-diff-driven feature since v1.46, running only changed test files and those importing changed files, making cheap dependency-graph selection table stakes.
records.applicability_limits: Import-graph selection misses runtime coupling through config, environment and generated code; a periodic full run remains the safety net.

records.finding: Specify the domain of valid inputs and the invariants that must hold, letting the tool generate cases, shrink counterexamples and persist failures for deterministic replay; one property test replaces many example tests where an invariant exists.
records.applicability_limits: Pays off only where a checkable invariant exists; much CRUD and UI code lacks one, and generation adds runtime cost and failure-triage effort.

records.finding: Mutation score (detected over valid mutants) measures whether tests actually detect faults, which line coverage cannot, and the killed/survived/no-coverage breakdown shows exactly which behaviours are unguarded.
records.applicability_limits: Equivalent mutants inflate scores, no target threshold is given, and full runs are expensive, so it is a periodic audit signal rather than a per-commit gate.

records.finding: Expensive quality audits become continuously affordable by diffing against a stored result file and re-running only mutants whose code or covering tests changed, while still emitting a full report.
records.applicability_limits: Diff-based reuse misses changes outside mutated and test files; maintainers recommend occasional forced full runs, and test-change detection quality varies by runner.

records.finding: Reliability targets are expressed as declarative vendor-neutral YAML objects (SLI, SLO, error budget, alert policy), making the target itself machine-readable and checkable rather than prose.
records.applicability_limits: A spec, not evidence that SLO-driven governance works; adoption breadth beyond observability vendors is unclear.

records.finding: A shared naming standard with explicit stability tiers lets the vocabulary widen coverage continuously while consumers know exactly which parts are safe to build on.
records.applicability_limits: Years of experimental-to-stable churn caused real migration pain; stability tiers defer but do not eliminate breaking change.

records.finding: A shared vocabulary evolves by versioned releases through an open community process with a small steering group, so consumers reference a release and the vocabulary grows without re-editing every consumer document.
records.applicability_limits: Governance is slow by design; demonstrates durability of versioned vocabularies more than speed.

records.version_or_commit: 3.x line current (3.1/3.2 published at spec.openapis.org); 4,385 commits
records.finding: A machine-readable interface contract lets humans and computers discover a service's capabilities without source access, while the spec stays deliberately process-agnostic between design-first and code-first.
records.applicability_limits: Contract-first benefits are widely asserted but the spec refuses to prescribe workflow; adoption evidence is ecosystem-scale rather than controlled.

records.finding: Contract-first extends to event-driven boundaries: machine-readable message and channel definitions agreed before implementation, from which code, docs and validation are generated.
records.applicability_limits: Younger and less universally adopted than OpenAPI; tooling coverage is uneven across protocols.

records.finding: One schema artefact serves as validation contract, annotation and documentation at once, so data-shape agreements are executable and fail loudly when reality diverges.
records.applicability_limits: Post-2020-12 stabilisation has been slow and expressiveness limits mean some business rules still need code.

records.finding: A vendor-agnostic flag evaluation API decouples deploy from release so risky behaviour ships dark, and its normative statements are parsed into machine-checkable JSON so conformance is testable rather than read.
records.applicability_limits: Standardises the interface only, not flag lifecycle hygiene; stale-flag debt is a known failure mode the spec does not address.

records.finding: Conformance is a set of technology-neutral, individually testable statements in tiered levels (A/AA/AAA), and criteria can be removed when they stop earning their keep, as 4.1.1 Parsing was in 2.2.
records.applicability_limits: Many real usability failures pass WCAG; the W3C acknowledges this through non-normative Understanding docs and the outcome-based WCAG 3 effort.

records.version_or_commit: unknown (2,167 commits on main at inspection)
records.licence: W3C licence (LICENSE.md present; exact variant not shown on landing page)
records.finding: Each pattern is an interaction contract of expected keyboard behaviour plus roles and states, independent of any visual system, so many house styles can conform to one behavioural spec.
records.applicability_limits: Guidance quality varies by pattern and assistive-technology support for some patterns remains inconsistent in practice.

records.finding: The APG declares itself neither prescriptive nor comprehensive: examples exist to teach and are not production code, with required invariants stated and the burden of testing on whoever deviates.
records.applicability_limits: Deliberate non-prescriptiveness pushes teams wanting copy-paste answers to Radix and design systems, which fragments practice.

records.source: Design Tokens Community Group format module
records.version_or_commit: spec release 2025.10 (28 October 2025); third editor's draft July 2025
records.licence: W3C Community Group licence (LICENSE.md present; variant not shown)
records.finding: Standardise the minimal interchange format of tokens, aliases and groups rather than the tools, so vendors compete on tooling while assets stay portable.
records.applicability_limits: Spent roughly five years in draft and a community-group report carries less force than a W3C Recommendation.

records.population: Python issue-reproduction tasks derived from SWE-bench
records.finding: Fail-to-pass reproduction-test generation from issues is the standard measure of agent testing ability and remains hard, with best 2025-era systems near 50 to 60% versus roughly 90% for patching.
records.applicability_limits: Python-only issue-reproduction framing derived from SWE-bench, sharing its repo-selection bias; SWT-Bench results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.population: 449 human-verified SWE-bench-derived instances
records.version_or_commit: main branch; companion Otter paper ICML 2025
records.finding: Tests generated from an issue before the patch exists can both enable TDD and validate agent patches, with fail-to-pass plus adequacy checks rather than coverage as the quality bar.
records.applicability_limits: Derived from SWE-bench Verified and measures test generation, not whether TDD improves the subsequent patching; benchmark results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.population: 647 curated from-scratch web-app generation cases
records.finding: For from-scratch web apps the discriminating quality signal is executable functional acceptance tests driven by a web-navigation agent, with the best framework at release passing only 27.8%, exposing failures static review misses.
records.applicability_limits: Test cases were authored via GPT-4o plus manual filtering, appearance scoring is subjective and scores rise quickly with newer models; WebGen-Bench results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.finding: Graded assurance levels are calibrated by risk-reduction per unit effort: v5 makes L1 roughly 20% of requirements as a realistic entry layer, L2 roughly 50% for most applications and L3 the final 30% for defence-in-depth.
records.applicability_limits: ASVS levels grade controls, not process ceremony, so mapping control tiers to workflow tiers is an analogy; tailoring still requires documented exclusions with rationale.

records.finding: Keep the barrier to entry deliberately low at the first tier and reserve expensive, hard-to-implement controls for the top tier, conceding that a perfect fit across contexts is impossible.
records.applicability_limits: The 20/50/30 percent-of-requirements framing is specific to a control catalogue; a process framework has no natural equivalent metric.

records.version_or_commit: v2.0 (v2.1 iterations exist; page shows v2)
records.finding: Maturity is measured per practice rather than globally, with 15 practices at three levels each, so an organisation can be mature in one practice and immature in another without a universal ceremony floor.
records.applicability_limits: A self-assessment model with soft scoring; nothing is gated mechanically and there is little controlled evidence SAMM scores predict fewer defects.

records.finding: Define outcomes at the practice level with a common vocabulary and let each implementation choose its own tooling and rigour, rather than mandating specific tools or a single methodology.
records.applicability_limits: High-level by design; gives no concrete gate placement or level scheme, so it constrains what to assure, not how much ceremony to spend.

records.licence: Community Specification License / CC (OpenSSF project); unknown exact
records.finding: Tracks with independent levels let you progress on one dimension without blocking on others, and verification sits at admission time against expectations rather than inside the producing workflow.
records.applicability_limits: SLSA measures pipeline tamper-resistance, not code quality; L3 needs build-platform features an agent framework cannot supply itself, and no guidance says which level to demand for a given risk.

records.finding: Keep doctrine as many small topic-scoped cross-indexed sheets with maintained index files mapping to the requirements standard, so breadth grows without any single document bloating and coverage gaps stay visible.
records.applicability_limits: Indexes are hand-maintained and the ASVS index still targets v4 mappings, illustrating semantic staleness that mechanical checks miss.

records.source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 and Generative AI Profile
records.finding: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage operate as continuous functions applied voluntarily and proportionally, with technology-specific profiles layered on a stable core rather than rewriting it.
records.applicability_limits: Entirely voluntary and abstract, with no controlled evidence linking adoption to outcomes; aimed at AI systems as products, so transfer to agents as workers is by analogy.

records.source: UK ICO guidance on AI and data protection
records.version_or_commit: updated 15 March 2023; under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act, 19 June 2025
records.licence: Open Government Licence (typical for ICO); unknown exact
records.finding: Ceremony scales with risk to people: DPIAs are mandatory only for high-risk processing, documentation is proportionate to that risk, and unresolvable residual high risk escalates to the regulator.
records.applicability_limits: Regulator guidance for personal-data processing under UK GDPR whose thresholds do not map to engineering-quality risk; explicitly in flux after the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

records.finding: The harness-editor boundary is a versioned JSON-RPC protocol surface in the LSP style, adopted by JetBrains, Google and over 25 agents, moving process into typed contracts rather than documents.
records.applicability_limits: A vendor-initiated de facto standard, not a standards-body artefact; adoption breadth verified only via secondary reporting.

records.finding: Client spans and metrics stabilised in early 2026 but agent spans remain in Development status, moved to a dedicated repository at v1.42.0 without a 1.0, so attribute names can still change without a major version bump.
records.applicability_limits: A direct corrective to building benchmark schemas on these attributes today; doing so buys churn until agent conventions stabilise.

records.finding: Agent guidance converges on one predictable plain-Markdown file with no required fields and proximity-based precedence, showing minimal schema beats elaborate mandatory structure for adoption.
records.applicability_limits: Adoption count is a popularity signal, not effectiveness evidence; the looseness offers no help with machine-readable state or ceremony grading.

records.version_or_commit: v0.19.2 (released 1 Aug, year rendered ambiguously by fetch; repo active as of Aug 2026)
records.finding: Minimal orchestration primitives (agent plus tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions) cover most multi-agent needs without an explicit graph, keeping control flow inside one coherent LLM run.
records.applicability_limits: Handoffs stay within a single run and guardrails only cover the first and last agents, so mid-chain coverage needs tool-level guardrails; pre-1.0 API churn is likely.

records.finding: Offer a ladder of orchestration: deterministic template agents for predictable pipelines, LLM-driven delegation for dynamic routing, and a full graph runtime only when needed.
records.applicability_limits: ADK 2.0 shipped breaking changes and its own docs now call template workflow agents the rigid option, showing these ladders churn; sessions are only backward-compatible to 1.28.

records.finding: Durable execution is a property of the boundary, not the worker: superstep checkpoints plus a request/response pattern make human-in-the-loop and crash recovery orthogonal to agent logic.
records.applicability_limits: Heavy Azure orientation and a graph API with real ceremony, which is why a lighter functional API ships alongside; 528 open issues at inspection.

records.version_or_commit: 1.2.10 (released 28 Jul, year rendered ambiguously by fetch; post-1.0 stable line, active Aug 2026)
records.finding: Per-thread checkpointing makes any run pausable, inspectable, editable and resumable, yet the maintainers steer simple cases to higher-level abstractions, conceding graph machinery only pays for long-running, durable, human-gated workflows.
records.applicability_limits: Interrupt semantics carry sharp edges: pre-interrupt code re-executes on resume so side effects must be idempotent, call order must be stable and payloads JSON-serialisable.

records.finding: A mature harness ships as a control plane over interchangeable agents and backends, with automation triggered by events and schedules; process lives in runtime machinery, not documents re-read each session.
records.applicability_limits: The README is marketing-level and run-loop internals live in the SDK repo, so this repo alone under-specifies the mechanisms.

records.version_or_commit: ~2,131 commits on main; unknown release tag
records.finding: The agent loop is a plain event-sourced conversation with pluggable condenser, security analyzer, stuck detector and confirmation policy, so safety and context hygiene are runtime services rather than procedural steps.
records.applicability_limits: Direct tool execution bypasses analyzers and confirmation, so the guarantees only hold inside the managed loop.

records.finding: The whole agent process is governed by a single YAML config and runs are bounded by budgets rather than phases, giving free-flowing agency within a hard resource envelope.
records.applicability_limits: Optimised for benchmark instances of one issue and one budget; less evidence for long multi-feature engagements, and superseded by mini-swe-agent for general use.

records.finding: Roughly 100 lines with bash as the only tool and strictly linear history reaches maintainer-reported results above 74% on SWE-bench Verified, suggesting strong models need budget and environment control, not procedural structure.
records.applicability_limits: The headline is maintainer-reported on SWE-bench Verified, a distribution of small localised bug fixes, and must not be promoted to universal doctrine; minimalism is less proven for large greenfield or multi-day work.
records.counter_evidence: OpenHands, at larger production scale, still invests in condensers, analyzers and delegation, so minimalism and rich runtime services coexist as valid poles.

records.source: Building a C compiler with Claude agent teams (Anthropic)
records.finding: A minimal loop with 16 parallel agents on a shared repo sustained a 100k-line project, with verifier quality the binding constraint: a near-perfect oracle plus parseable test output let agents self-direct without an orchestrator.
records.applicability_limits: Compilers have an unusually clean oracle that most product work lacks; regressions were frequent, so high parallelism without strong regression suites degrades quality.

records.version_or_commit: main branch, ~46 commits as of 2026-08-02; spec mirrored at agentskills.io (no version number stated)
records.licence: Apache-2.0 for most skills; document skills (docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx) source-available, non-open-source
records.finding: Capability is packaged as self-contained skill directories with progressive disclosure keeping cost near zero until needed: about 100 tokens of metadata always loaded, the body on activation, references on demand.
records.applicability_limits: The spec fixes format, not efficacy; no published evidence on how much skill packaging improves task success versus inlined instructions, and allowed-tools is experimental.

records.finding: The handbook is the single source of truth and the working artefact itself: changes go handbook-first via merge request and gaps are fixed at the point of discovery, so freshness is a by-product of doing work.
records.applicability_limits: GitLab is thousands of humans; the cost model of merge-request review for every doc change may not transfer to a solo-operator agent estate, and freshness claims are self-reported.

records.finding: Quality rules are declarative Expectations that are simultaneously the test and the documentation, with validation results auto-generating data docs so documentation cannot silently diverge from what is checked.
records.applicability_limits: Expectation suites go stale if data semantics drift in unasserted ways; the tool checks what you declared, not what you forgot to declare.

records.finding: Freeze only the interface: enforced contracts guarantee column names, types and constraints of public models at build time while internals refactor freely, and private models carry no contract ceremony.
records.applicability_limits: Contract enforcement covers shape, not meaning, and dbt pairs contracts with versions and access modifiers, which adds its own ceremony.

records.finding: Golden-path templates encode best practice at creation time: the scaffolder stamps out a compliant skeleton and auto-registers it in the catalog, so ownership records are created by the tool.
records.applicability_limits: Catalog freshness still depends on files being updated on change; Spotify concedes golden paths need continual gardening or they rot.

records.licence: unknown (GrowthBook core is MIT; EDF is a Pro/Enterprise feature)
records.finding: Asymmetric gating: goal metrics drive ship decisions while guardrail metrics only block on statistically significant harm, and automated recommendations fire once a pre-declared precision target is reached.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor documentation of its own feature; the defaults are conventions, not validated optima.

records.finding: A deliberately tiny standard set of user-centric metrics with published thresholds makes quality benchmarkable across every project without bespoke measurement design.
records.applicability_limits: Thresholds are Google-set conventions for the web; the transferable idea is the small fixed metric set, and lab and field scores routinely disagree.

records.finding: Rolling date-based versions with consumers pinned to their integration version and each breaking change encapsulated as a self-contained transformation module kept every version since 2011 working through roughly 100 incompatible upgrades.
records.applicability_limits: One company's account of its own system; the version-module machinery has real engineering cost and pays off only at high consumer count.

records.version_or_commit: unknown (7,335 commits on main at inspection)
records.licence: MIT (code); docs under Open Government Licence 3.0
records.finding: Guidance and governance live in a repo separate from implementation code, so process docs and reusable assets evolve on independent cadences without churning each other.
records.applicability_limits: Government context with a dedicated full-time team and a single dominant brand; the separation costs more for small estates.

records.finding: Graded compatibility instead of binary support: browser grades A to X state exactly how much is promised to each consumer tier, and semantic versioning plus deprecation guidance lets services lag safely.
records.applicability_limits: Release details were not visible on the landing page and graded support adds a test-matrix cost.

records.finding: Tokens are unlocked through functions and a single theme settings layer rather than consumed as raw values, keeping system structure invariant while agencies customise.
records.applicability_limits: Claims WCAG 2.0 AA conformance, an older baseline than 2.2, and the Sass-function token API has a reported steep learning curve.

records.applicability_limits: DTCG-format support was not confirmed from the landing page and the build-pipeline model adds a compile step with ongoing edge cases.

records.finding: Headless separation ships behaviour and accessibility as an invariant tested core with zero visual opinion, so every consumer gets the hard correctness properties for free.
records.applicability_limits: Corporate single-sponsor maintenance is a bus-factor risk, with community concerns about issue backlog and release cadence.

records.finding: Distribute reference implementations you copy and own rather than a dependency you conform to: consumers vendor the code and never wait on upstream, so the system is a seed, not a governor.
records.applicability_limits: Vendoring forfeits upstream fixes, so security and accessibility patches must be re-applied by hand; popularity is not controlled evidence of quality.

records.finding: Replace standing secrets and manual attestations with ephemeral identity plus an append-only transparency log, so the audit trail is a by-product of the act rather than a maintained document.
records.applicability_limits: Assumes an OIDC identity provider and public log infrastructure, with a weaker private-log story; adoption evidence is ecosystem-scale, not controlled.

records.finding: Repository health is scored automatically and continuously by 23 risk-weighted checks that read the repo's actual state rather than its self-description, with structured results consumable by policy.
records.applicability_limits: Checks are heuristics on repo metadata that can be gamed or misfire; they measure hygiene, not semantic correctness or staleness of docs.

records.finding: Encode review policy as executable rules that look like the code, run diff-aware in CI so only issues introduced by the pull request are reported, split findings into blocking versus monitor, and attach autofixes for trivial findings.
records.applicability_limits: Community Edition is intra-file only and the vendor states it has limitations for security work; autofix covers mechanical patterns, not design-level repairs.

records.finding: Decouple policy from the thing governed: systems query a general-purpose engine with structured input and get a decision back, so policy is versioned, tested and changed centrally.
records.applicability_limits: Rego has a real learning curve, and policy-as-code only helps when the inputs are machine-readable, which a prose-based process estate lacks.

records.finding: The industry is converging on asynchronous agent fleets governed at the platform layer, with mission control assigning work to heterogeneous agents and delivering results as pull requests.
records.applicability_limits: A vendor platform announcement whose throughput and quality claims are unaudited, and it locks governance into GitHub's control plane.

records.applicability_limits: Still benchmarks model plus harness on public tasks, which invite contamination; it does not measure doctrine or process variants on private venture work, and Terminal-Bench results must not be promoted to universal doctrine.

records.version_or_commit: release tag ~v0.12.11, ~1,681 commits on main (as of 2026-08-02)
records.finding: Decompose work into a fixed artifact chain (constitution, spec, plan, tasks) where each layer strips detail the next needs, with consistency checked by a command rather than by re-reading everything.
records.applicability_limits: Positioned mainly for greenfield work with no documented reduced-ceremony path, and no controlled evidence the pipeline improves throughput or quality.

records.finding: Specs are living artifacts with production learnings fed back and downstream artefacts regenerated, and gates sit at phase boundaries with exceptions allowed but logged, giving graded rather than absolute enforcement.
records.applicability_limits: The code-is-disposable claim is aspirational and unvalidated at scale, and the essay prescribes test-first as a constitutional article as broadly as any doctrine it replaces.

records.finding: Run cheap checks in parallel with the expensive work and abort via tripwire only when they fire, reserving blocking mode for cases where wasted tokens genuinely matter.
records.applicability_limits: Parallel mode can consume tokens before the guardrail trips, trading some waste for latency; not a substitute for output verification.

records.finding: Reserve determinism for the parts of a process that must be repeatable (order, retries, termination) and let the model own everything inside each step; routing belongs to the step boundary, not the whole system.
records.applicability_limits: Docs are thin on state-sharing mechanics and evaluation claims are not independently verified.

records.finding: Ship two entry points to one runtime: a functional API for sequential and ad-hoc work and a graph builder only for fixed topologies, both with identical observability, human-in-the-loop and checkpoint behaviour.
records.applicability_limits: The functional API is marked experimental in Python and the equivalence claim is the vendor's own.

records.finding: Human review is modelled as pause-with-payload and resume-with-value at a named point backed by the checkpointer, so gates go where risk is rather than at fixed phase boundaries.
records.applicability_limits: Requires a durable checkpointer and thread IDs, persistent infrastructure a docs-only estate lacks; the pattern transfers, the mechanism does not.

records.finding: Context is managed automatically by a summarising condenser that fires past an event threshold while always preserving the first events, with a claimed cost reduction of up to 2x per turn at equivalent task performance.
records.applicability_limits: The cost and quality claim is maintainer-reported, not an independent controlled study.

records.finding: Risk is assessed per action by composable analyzers ensembled by taking the maximum, while a separate confirmation policy decides gating, decoupling analysis from enforcement.
records.applicability_limits: LLM risk annotation depends on model judgment and direct tool execution bypasses the whole apparatus.

records.finding: Unproductive loops are detected mechanically by semantic comparison of recent events (repeated action-observation, action-error, monologue and ping-pong patterns) and halt the run by default.
records.applicability_limits: Documented false positives include agents killed while legitimately polling long-running processes; thresholds tuned for weaker models can harm strong ones.

records.finding: Standing knowledge is delivered by progressive disclosure: names and descriptions load up front, full content injects only on keyword trigger, and only repo-wide conventions are always-on.
records.applicability_limits: Keyword triggering can miss relevant knowledge when phrasing differs; no semantic matching is described.

records.finding: Parallelism is achieved by delegation rather than role ceremony: a main agent spawns sub-agents with isolated conversation contexts that return results for consolidation.
records.applicability_limits: Delegation isolates context but merge quality is the parent's problem, with no documented conflict resolution between parallel sub-agents.

records.finding: Split long work into a one-off initialiser agent and a repeated coding agent whose every session starts from git log and progress artifacts, because structured artifacts, not compaction alone, carry continuity across context windows.
records.applicability_limits: Single case-study guidance on web-app building with Opus 4.5, with no controlled comparison; the March 2026 follow-up shows parts of this scaffolding became unnecessary as models improved.

records.source: Effective context engineering for AI agents (Anthropic)
records.finding: Treat context as a finite resource with diminishing returns: pitch prompts at the right altitude, and for long horizons use compaction, structured notes, condensed sub-agent returns and just-in-time retrieval instead of pre-loading everything.
records.applicability_limits: Qualitative guidance from Anthropic's own experience, with no quantitative thresholds for when compaction, notes or sub-agents win.

records.finding: Start evals early with 20 to 50 tasks harvested from real failures, use pass@k and pass^k for non-determinism, mix code graders, model graders and human transcript review, and keep validating the graders themselves.
records.applicability_limits: A how-to synthesis, not controlled evidence; grader-design advice is heuristic and the article warns of eval saturation and grading bugs.

records.finding: Distinguish workflows (predefined code paths for well-defined tasks) from agents (model directs its own process for open-ended problems), and start with the simplest thing that works, adding composable patterns only when measured need justifies them.
records.applicability_limits: Written for the weaker 2024 model generation; later Anthropic posts show the workflow-agent boundary shifting toward more autonomy as models improve.

records.source: Harness design for long-running application development (Anthropic)
records.finding: Every harness component encodes an assumption about what the model cannot do, so strip scaffolding as models improve; keep evaluation separate from generation because agents praise their own work, and make evaluators verify actively.
records.applicability_limits: A single-author experiment on app development; the planner-generator-evaluator separation is defended for self-assessment bias, with capability-dependent scaffold removal as the resolution.

records.finding: Tests should assert user-visible behaviour, be fully isolated, mock third-party services at the network layer, and rely on auto-retrying web-first assertions with parallelism as the default.
records.applicability_limits: Guidance is end-to-end specific, and avoiding implementation details is a philosophy claim rather than controlled evidence.

records.finding: Replace integrated end-to-end environments with consumer-driven contracts verified independently on each side plus a machine-answerable deploy gate, adopted in stages so partial adoption still pays.
records.applicability_limits: Contract tests verify message shape and known interactions, not emergent whole-system behaviour; the claim of eliminating E2E tests is aspirational and contested for UI flows.

records.finding: The more tests resemble the way software is used, the more confidence they give: test through the interface users see, never through implementation internals, so refactors do not break tests that should pass.
records.applicability_limits: A design philosophy, not controlled evidence; behaviour-level tests can be slower and give coarser failure localisation than unit tests.

records.finding: Prefer real dependencies in throwaway per-run containers over mocks that behave slightly differently and shared environments that drift, making integration tests as runnable locally as unit tests.
records.applicability_limits: Requires Docker everywhere tests run; containerised dependencies are slower than in-memory fakes and cannot exactly emulate managed cloud services.

records.source: Write tests. Not too many. Mostly integration. (Kent C. Dodds)
records.finding: Optimise for confidence per test rather than layer ratios: integration tests give the best return, and coverage past roughly 70% has diminishing returns for applications.
records.applicability_limits: Maintainer opinion, front-end skewed, with no controlled evidence.
records.counter_evidence: Contradicts the classic Cohn test pyramid that many organisations still standardise on.

records.finding: Docs stay fresh through edit-on-encounter: a missing answer is immediately PRed into the place you looked, and substantive decisions live in PRs and issues so the record writes itself.
records.applicability_limits: Company self-description with no measurement of how often edit-on-encounter actually happens versus decay.

records.source: Google SRE Workbook error budget policy
records.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (published free online; verify before reuse)
records.finding: An error budget converts a reliability target into a governance dial: while budget remains teams ship with low ceremony, and when it is spent changes halt except P0 and security until back within SLO.
records.applicability_limits: Google-scale practice with no controlled comparison; licence is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so paraphrase only, no verbatim reuse in EOS documents.

records.finding: Decision records scale with the decision: full, minimal and bare templates let a record be three lines or three pages, and only decisions that matter get one, making ceremony opt-in per decision.
records.applicability_limits: Community convention with no measured evidence ADRs improve outcomes; template proliferation becomes ceremony if mandated for every choice.

records.finding: A one-page canvas with fixed prompts captures a context's design at workshop speed, forcing explicit choices without exhaustive documentation.
records.applicability_limits: Designed for human workshops; no evidence it works as an agent-readable artefact without adaptation.

records.finding: Naming the relationship between modules explicitly makes integration cost and change-propagation direction visible, via several small maps answering specific questions rather than one monolithic diagram.
records.applicability_limits: Patterns are anecdotal, from Evans and practitioner experience, and the maintainers themselves flag the technique as unnecessary below a complexity threshold.

records.finding: Modelling is explicitly non-linear beginner scaffolding, with coding before architecture confirmation sanctioned and discovery continuous rather than a phase.
records.applicability_limits: Self-declared beginner scaffolding whose maintainers warn against institutionalising it, which cuts against embedding any fixed modelling pipeline in doctrine.

records.finding: Hierarchical zoom with deliberately diminishing obligation: context and container views are the workhorses, and component diagrams are created only if they add value, ideally automated.
records.applicability_limits: A single-author practice framework with no controlled study of comprehension benefit; lower levels are rarely worth manual upkeep by the author's own admission.

records.licence: unknown (Apache-2.0 for structurizr/dsl historically; not confirmed on the docs page)
records.finding: Models as code rather than diagrams as code: one text-based version-controlled model generates many views that never drift from each other, and derived diagrams are regenerated, never hand-edited.
records.applicability_limits: Requires learning a DSL and model-first discipline collapses if people edit rendered outputs; same single-author lineage as C4.

records.source: GOV.UK community backlog and component criteria
records.finding: New components enter the system only through an evidence gate of designs, code or research findings, with priority to patterns already used across multiple services, so guidance follows demonstrated usage.
records.applicability_limits: The evidence gate is slow by design and informally criticised for lag between service need and published pattern.

records.finding: The build artifact is the test case: every story is automatically a render test, play functions add interaction tests and the a11y addon runs axe checks in the same loop, embedding verification in the act of building.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor docs promote the maintainer's paid visual-regression service, and axe-style automated checks catch only the machine-detectable subset of accessibility failures, commonly cited as roughly a third.

records.source: Mutation-Guided LLM Test Generation at Meta (ACES)
records.population: Meta production apps, Q4 2024 deployment
records.finding: At production scale, mutation score rather than coverage percentage is the actionable quality signal: mutation-guided generation targeted undetected faults and engineers accepted 73% of generated tests.
records.applicability_limits: An industrial deployment report, not a controlled comparison, on Meta-specific infrastructure; related academic work finds LLM tests miss boundary-killing assertions and sometimes assert training-data expectations.

records.finding: Parallel multi-agent systems fail through fragmented context and conflicting decisions; context engineering with a single coherent thread of actions is more reliable than parallel actors.
records.applicability_limits: Production experience from one vendor with no controlled comparison; the author has since partially revised the position.
records.counter_evidence: Cognition's own April 2026 follow-up identifies three multi-agent patterns that survive in production when writes stay single-threaded.

records.finding: Multi-agent setups that survive in production keep writes single-threaded while extra agents contribute intelligence rather than actions, with Code-Review-Loop, Smart Friend and map-reduce-and-manage the three surviving patterns.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor practice rather than controlled evidence, and it contradicts more parallelism-optimistic framings elsewhere.

records.finding: The runtime now ships coordination primitives an EOS would otherwise document by hand (shared task lists with dependencies, mailboxes, lifecycle hooks, per-teammate plan approval), and its own guidance is conservative: 3 to 5 teammates with disjoint file ownership.
records.applicability_limits: Experimental and disabled by default, with no session resumption for in-process teammates, lagging task status and per-teammate token cost; vendor docs with no published outcome data.

records.source: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST taxonomy)
records.study_design: empirical failure-mode taxonomy from expert annotation of execution traces, with inter-annotator agreement study
records.population: 1600+ annotated traces across 7 popular multi-agent frameworks, 6 expert annotators, 200+ tasks
records.benchmark: coding, maths and general agent tasks
records.version_or_commit: arXiv v3, 26 Oct 2025; NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks track
records.finding: Multi-agent failures are dominated by specification gaps, inter-agent misalignment and absent task verification rather than raw model weakness, and the categories were reproducible at kappa 0.88, so a topology choice must be justified against a named failure mode it removes.
records.applicability_limits: Traces come from 2024-2025 framework generations and older models, so absolute failure rates will have moved; the taxonomy is diagnostic, it does not prove any particular topology is better.
records.counter_evidence: Anthropic's orchestrator-worker research system reports a large uplift from parallel subagents on breadth-first search tasks, so multi-agent failure is conditional on task shape, not universal.

records.source: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
records.study_design: system paper with ablations over interface design choices
records.population: SWE-bench and HumanEvalFix instances
records.model: GPT-4 Turbo and Claude models of the 2024 generation
records.finding: The interface an agent acts through is a first-class design surface: purpose-built commands with concise, informative feedback and guardrails against malformed edits changed task success far more than prompt wording, so tool ergonomics are engineering work, not glue.
records.applicability_limits: Numbers are from the 2024 model generation and are now far below the state of the art; the principle transfers, the specific interface and scores do not.
records.counter_evidence: mini-swe-agent (EV-0052) reaches much higher scores with bash as the only tool, suggesting stronger models need less bespoke interface scaffolding.

records.source: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
records.study_design: controlled comparison of intrinsic self-correction against baselines on reasoning benchmarks
records.population: standard reasoning benchmark question sets under a fixed evaluation setup
records.model: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 class models of 2023-2024
records.finding: Without external feedback, models asked to review and revise their own answers often degrade them, so an evaluator-optimizer loop only pays when the evaluator holds ground truth the generator lacks, such as tests, types, linters or a separate context.
records.applicability_limits: Studies short-form reasoning on the 2023-2024 generation, not long-horizon coding where compilers and test suites supply exactly the external signal the paper says is missing.
records.counter_evidence: Anthropic's C compiler experiment (EV-0053) shows self-directed agents improving reliably when a near-perfect external oracle is present, which is consistent rather than contradictory.

records.source: How we built our multi-agent research system (Anthropic)
records.model: Claude Opus 4 lead, Claude Sonnet 4 subagents
records.finding: Orchestrator-worker fan-out pays only where subtasks are separable and read-only: the vendor reports a 90.2% uplift over a single agent on breadth-first research at roughly fifteen times the token cost, and states the pattern suits neither shared-context work nor most coding.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor-reported internal evaluation on open-ended search, not code change; the token multiple makes the pattern uneconomic for narrow tasks and the post lists subagent over-spawning and duplicated work as recurring failures.
records.counter_evidence: Cognition (EV-0106) argues fragmented context makes parallel actors unreliable; the two reconcile only if parallel agents read and the parent writes.

records.source: Writing effective tools for AI agents (Anthropic)
records.benchmark: internal Slack and Asana tool evaluations
records.finding: Tools are a contract between a deterministic system and a non-deterministic caller: consolidate them around whole workflows rather than API endpoints, namespace them, return high-signal semantic content instead of identifiers, and treat token efficiency and description wording as tunable through evaluation.
records.applicability_limits: Guidance is qualitative with the strongest quantitative claims held internal; the post warns namespacing effects vary by model and there is no universal best response format.

records.finding: Tool surface is a context cost: presenting servers as a browsable code API so definitions and intermediate results load on demand cut one worked example from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens, making progressive disclosure the default for large tool estates.
records.applicability_limits: The 98.7% figure is a single illustrative scenario, not a measured distribution, and the approach requires a sandboxed execution environment with resource limits, which is itself a security surface.

records.source: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK (Anthropic)
records.finding: The unit of agent design is the loop gather context, take action, verify work, and action capability should be chosen in the order explicit tools, bash, generated code, then MCP; verification should prefer defined rules and visual feedback over a model judge.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor guidance tuned to one SDK and to Claude models, with the ordering asserted rather than measured; the LLM-judge caveat is acknowledged in the source itself.

records.source: OpenAI Agents SDK orchestration guide (LLM versus code)
records.finding: Split orchestration explicitly into model-driven and code-driven, and inside model-driven distinguish agents-as-tools (specialist helps with a bounded subtask, caller keeps the conversation) from handoffs (routing is the workflow and the specialist owns what follows).
records.applicability_limits: Vendor framing without outcome data; the four code patterns named (structured-output routing, chaining, evaluator loop, parallel gather) are illustrative, not exhaustive.

records.source: OpenAI Agents SDK sessions and compaction docs
records.finding: Conversation memory is a swappable store behind one interface (SQLite, Redis, SQLAlchemy, MongoDB, server-side, encrypted), with retrieval limits, a compaction wrapper and a per-run input callback, so trimming policy is configuration rather than agent logic.
records.applicability_limits: Sessions are mutually exclusive with server-side conversation ids, auto-compaction can block streaming, and the store gives recall not relevance; no retrieval-quality claims are made.

records.finding: Tracing should be on by default with a fixed span vocabulary (run, turn, agent, generation, tool, guardrail, handoff), a workflow name and a group id linking related runs, plus a switch that keeps spans while excluding inputs and outputs when data policy forbids them.
records.applicability_limits: The default backend is the vendor's own and is unusable under zero-data-retention; portability rests on third-party processors rather than a native OpenTelemetry emitter.

records.version_or_commit: ADK docs current 2026-08-03; callbacks since Python v0.1.0
records.finding: Six symmetric interception points (before and after agent, model and tool) with three uniform outcomes (continue, override and short-circuit, modify in flight) give guardrails, caching and state edits one predictable shape instead of bespoke wrappers per concern.
records.applicability_limits: Callbacks bind to a single agent instance, and the docs themselves redirect security guardrails to plugins, so callback-level enforcement does not compose across a system.

records.version_or_commit: ADK docs current 2026-08-03; plugins since Python v1.7.0
records.finding: Cross-cutting policy belongs at the runner, not the agent: plugins register once, cover the whole run including error hooks, and take precedence over per-agent callbacks, which is what makes a guardrail non-bypassable by any single agent's configuration.
records.applicability_limits: Precedence is also a hazard, since a plugin returning a value silently skips agent-level callbacks; version floors differ across language SDKs.

records.source: Microsoft Agent Framework workflow checkpoints docs
records.version_or_commit: doc git commit b4add1d, ms.date 2026-05-27, updated 2026-07-10
records.finding: Checkpoint at a defined barrier rather than at arbitrary points: at each superstep boundary the framework saves executor state, pending messages, pending requests and shared state, so a run can resume in place or rehydrate into a fresh process, and participants must implement explicit save and restore hooks.
records.applicability_limits: Python file and Cosmos stores use pickle behind a restricted unpickler, so checkpoint storage is a trust boundary and untrusted checkpoints must never be loaded; durability depends on the store chosen.

records.source: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
records.version_or_commit: RFC 9457, July 2023, Standards Track, obsoletes RFC 7807
records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions (BSD-style, RFC text)
records.finding: Errors are part of the contract: carry a stable machine-readable type URI plus human detail in one agreed media type, so a consumer branches on the type rather than on prose or on the bare status code.
records.applicability_limits: Defines a container, not the taxonomy; the type URIs and their stability are still the API owner's design work. Adds a second media type to negotiate, which is friction for tiny internal APIs.
records.counter_evidence: Microsoft Azure guidelines mandate a different, incompatible error envelope (error.code / error.message plus x-ms-error-code header) rather than problem+json, showing large estates diverge from the RFC.

records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions (BSD-style, RFC text)
records.finding: A signature is only as good as its base string: canonicalise an explicit, ordered list of covered components (fields plus derived values such as method, path, authority) so signer and verifier build byte-identical input despite lawful intermediary rewriting, and bind created, expires and nonce for replay control.
records.applicability_limits: Covers request and response signing generally, not webhook delivery specifically; requires a canonicalisation library on both sides and is heavier than a single HMAC-over-raw-body scheme. Adoption outside standards-conscious estates is still thin.
records.counter_evidence: Standard Webhooks and GitHub both ship simpler HMAC-over-a-fixed-string schemes rather than RFC 9421, and dominate real webhook traffic.

records.source: RFC 9745 The Deprecation HTTP Response Header Field
records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions (BSD-style, RFC text)
records.finding: Deprecation is announced in-band and dated, and removal is a separate later date: Deprecation carries when the resource became or becomes deprecated, RFC 8594 Sunset carries when it stops responding, and Sunset must not be earlier than Deprecation.
records.applicability_limits: Informational only, it changes no behaviour, so it works solely if consumers instrument for it. Says nothing about how long the gap between the two dates should be.

records.version_or_commit: spec version 1.0.0, main branch as at 2026-08-03
records.finding: Sign the triple id.timestamp.payload, not the payload alone: the id gives the consumer a natural idempotency key, the timestamp gives a replay window, and the versioned signature prefix (v1 HMAC-SHA256, v1a ed25519) plus multi-signature headers give zero-downtime key rotation. Constant-time comparison and signing exactly the bytes transmitted are mandatory.
records.applicability_limits: Does not fix a numeric timestamp tolerance, so each estate must pick one. Payload guidance (type, timestamp, data; under about 20kb) is a convention, not enforceable. Vendor-originated (Svix) despite the neutral name.
records.counter_evidence: GitHub, Stripe and Slack each ship incompatible bespoke schemes; there is no convergence in practice, so a consumer library must still special-case per provider.

records.finding: Verify against the raw request body before any parsing or re-encoding, and compare digests in constant time; a framework that hands you a parsed object has already destroyed the bytes the signature covers.
records.applicability_limits: One vendor's scheme, with no timestamp header and therefore no built-in replay window; the raw-body and constant-time lessons generalise, the header layout does not.

records.version_or_commit: draft-07, intended status Standards Track, expiry 2026-04-18; no RFC number as at 2026-08-03
records.finding: A client-generated Idempotency-Key request header makes POST and PATCH fault-tolerant, moving retry safety from server-side guesswork to an explicit contract term the client controls.
records.applicability_limits: Still an expired-window Internet-Draft after several years, so the header name is de facto rather than de jure; do not cite it as a ratified standard. Says nothing binding about retention windows or conflict semantics.
records.counter_evidence: Microsoft Azure guidelines instead mandate OASIS Repeatable Requests headers (Repeatability-Request-ID, Repeatability-First-Sent), so the header name is genuinely contested at scale.

records.version_or_commit: draft-11 dated 2026-05-23, intended status Standards Track, expiry 2026-11-24; no RFC number as at 2026-08-03
records.finding: Split the static quota policy (RateLimit-Policy) from the live remaining budget (RateLimit) so a client can plan its call pattern in advance rather than discovering limits only by being refused.
records.applicability_limits: Draft, not an RFC, and the field syntax has churned across eleven revisions; pinning to a specific draft number is required for interoperability. Advisory only, it does not define enforcement or 429 behaviour.

records.finding: Compatibility is three separate guarantees that must each hold: source, wire and semantic. Renaming is removal plus addition and therefore breaking; so are moving a field into or out of a oneof, changing a type, changing a default, changing a resource-name format, and adding a required request field.
records.applicability_limits: Written for protobuf-shaped APIs at Google scale; the semantic-compatibility bar (no change to how a value is constructed) is stricter than most estates can afford. Enum additions are flagged as risky rather than forbidden, which leaves a judgement call.

records.finding: Page tokens must be opaque and non-parseable, must bind to the filter and ordering of the call that issued them (mismatched follow-up parameters are an INVALID_ARGUMENT error), must never carry authorisation, and total counts are optional and may be an estimate.
records.applicability_limits: Opacity forbids the client-side tricks (jump to page N, resume from an arbitrary offset) that some consumers expect; suits list-and-stream consumption, not table UIs that need page numbers.
records.counter_evidence: JSON:API reserves a page parameter family but deliberately stays strategy-agnostic, so offset paging remains conformant there.

records.version_or_commit: web edition as served 2026-08-03, targeting OpenAPI 3.1
records.finding: A working corporate rulebook is a graded one: MUST for API-first definition in OpenAPI before code, no URL versioning, media-type versioning, no backward-incompatible change and problem+json errors; SHOULD for cursor pagination and idempotent POST/PATCH via an Idempotency-Key. The MUST list is short enough to be enforceable.
records.applicability_limits: Media-type versioning is a minority position and is poorly supported by browsers, caches and casual clients; adopting it wholesale imports tooling pain. Written for a large multi-team retailer, so the review ceremony does not fit a small estate.
records.counter_evidence: Microsoft Azure guidelines mandate an api-version query parameter, directly contradicting both URL and media-type positions, and are equally battle-tested.

records.licence: unknown (repository licence file not inspected; repo commonly Apache-2.0 or CC-BY-4.0)
records.finding: Make the version explicit and mandatory rather than defaulted: a required api-version query parameter using YYYY-MM-DD with a -preview suffix, a 400 with a named error code when it is missing or unknown, error codes treated as contract (a new top-level code needs a version bump), and slow calls promoted to long-running operations with a 202 plus operation-location status monitor retained at least 24 hours.
records.applicability_limits: Mandatory-version-parameter and LRO machinery presume a large managed-service estate with generated SDKs; both are heavy for an internal API with two consumers. Rejecting a call for a missing api-version is hostile to exploratory clients.
records.counter_evidence: Zalando forbids URL versioning and mandates media-type versioning; Stripe (EV-0061) uses an account-pinned date header. Three mature estates, three incompatible answers.

records.finding: Idempotency needs four decided parameters, not one header: the stored result is the status code and body of the first attempt including 5xx; retention is at least 24 hours after which the same key starts a fresh request; replaying a key with different parameters is an error, not a silent overwrite; and a request conflicting with a concurrently executing one is not cached and is safe to retry.
records.applicability_limits: Applies to POST only, since GET and DELETE are idempotent by definition. Caching a 500 means a client that retries a genuinely transient failure with the same key gets the failure back forever, which pushes retry-with-new-key policy onto the client.

records.finding: A media type can evolve without a version negotiation mechanism at all if it commits publicly to never remove, only add; JSON:API makes that the governing rule and keeps its version field optional as a result.
records.applicability_limits: Never-remove is affordable for a wire format with no business semantics; a product API accumulating dead fields forever pays a real comprehension and maintenance cost. The document conventions (type/id/relationships/included) are opinionated and unsuited to non-resource-shaped domains.
records.counter_evidence: Stripe (EV-0061) demonstrates the opposite bet: roughly a hundred deliberate incompatible changes survived only because version transformation modules were built to absorb them.

records.finding: Compatibility is not binary but a chosen strictness tier, and the tier should be declared: FILE (default, protects generated code layout), PACKAGE, WIRE_JSON (minimum where JSON transports are used), WIRE (binary only). Start strict and relax deliberately rather than discovering the tier by breaking someone.
records.applicability_limits: Protobuf-specific; the tier vocabulary does not map cleanly onto JSON-over-HTTP, where there is no equivalent of generated-file placement. Requires a stored baseline to diff against.

records.version_or_commit: main branch, 1,892 commits, approx 1.3k stars, as at 2026-08-03
records.finding: Breaking-change detection can be mechanised against the spec itself: a breaking command gates the build, a separate changelog command reports consumer-visible but non-breaking changes, and the classification rules are configurable rather than hard-coded, so an estate can encode its own compatibility promise.
records.applicability_limits: Detects only what the spec expresses; semantic breaks that leave the schema unchanged (a field's meaning or units altered) pass silently. Requires a committed baseline spec and therefore only works where the spec is generated or authored reliably.

records.version_or_commit: develop branch, 2,239 commits, approx 3.2k stars, as at 2026-08-03; supports OpenAPI 2/3.0/3.1, AsyncAPI 2.x, Arazzo 1.0
records.finding: API conventions only bind if they are executable: a ruleset turns house style (naming, required descriptions, error shapes, forbidden patterns) into a lint run that fails, which is the difference between a guideline document and governance.
records.applicability_limits: No OpenAPI 3.2 support listed as at the access date, which matters if the pack standardises on 3.2. Linting checks form, never behaviour, so a lint-clean spec can still describe a service that does something else.

records.version_or_commit: v1.0.2 latest release; 1,124 commits on main; CNCF graduated 2024-01-25
records.finding: Standardise the event envelope (id, source, type, specversion, time) separately from the payload, so routing, deduplication and tracing work across transports without every consumer relearning a bespoke metadata layout.
records.applicability_limits: Governs metadata only; payload schema and its evolution remain entirely the producer's problem, which is where most event breakage actually happens. Version has sat at 1.0.2 for a long stretch, so treat it as stable rather than evolving.

records.source: Confluent Schema Registry schema evolution and compatibility
records.finding: For event contracts the compatibility mode encodes an upgrade order and must be chosen before the first schema change: BACKWARD (default, consumers first), FORWARD (producers first), FULL (either order, add or remove optional fields only), NONE (lockstep). Transitive variants check every prior version, not just the last, which is the only mode safe for replayable logs.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor documentation for one registry; the mode names are Confluent's, though the underlying upgrade-order logic is general. Non-transitive modes give a false sense of safety when consumers rewind a topic to its start.

records.version_or_commit: September2025 edition current release; prerelease working draft dated 2026-04-02
records.licence: unknown (spec text served under an Open Web Foundation agreement; licence page not retrieved)
records.finding: GraphQL replaces API versioning with continuous schema evolution: fields are added freely and retired via deprecation because a client only receives what it explicitly selected, so additions cannot break existing queries.
records.applicability_limits: The spec text itself returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval at the access date, so the edition and date come from the publisher's version index rather than the document. The no-versioning claim holds for field additions and holds much less for type, nullability or argument changes.
records.counter_evidence: Never removing fields means schemas accrete indefinitely; deprecation without a sunset date is not removal, so the version problem is deferred rather than solved.

records.source: Brito and Valente, REST vs GraphQL: A Controlled Experiment
records.study_design: Within-subjects controlled experiment; 22 participants (10 undergraduate, 12 graduate) each implemented eight queries against a web service using both GraphQL and REST
records.population: 22 university students, ICSA 2020
records.finding: GraphQL reduced client query implementation effort against REST (median 6 minutes versus 9), and the gap widened for REST endpoints with several parameters; the benefit held for participants with REST but no GraphQL experience.
records.applicability_limits: Students, not professionals; measures first-write time for eight queries only, and says nothing about server implementation cost, operational cost, caching, authorisation or long-term maintenance, which is where GraphQL's real bill arrives.
records.counter_evidence: The single measured dimension (client authoring time) is the dimension GraphQL is designed to optimise; the experiment does not measure the server-side and security costs that drive most GraphQL regret.

records.source: Zetterlund, Tiwari, Monperrus and Baudry, Harvesting Production GraphQL Queries to Detect Schema Faults
records.study_design: Tool construction (AutoGraphQL) plus empirical evaluation against two production GraphQL applications
records.population: Two production GraphQL APIs (Saleor e-commerce, Frontapp)
records.finding: Tests derived from real production queries covered 26.9 percent of the Saleor schema and 48.7 percent of the Frontapp schema and found eight schema faults, exercising parts of the API the developers' own suites never touched.
records.applicability_limits: Two applications only, and GraphQL-specific. The low coverage figures are the point: a permissive schema surface far exceeds what any consumer actually exercises, so most of a large GraphQL schema is effectively untested attack surface.

records.source: Hatfield-Dodds and Dygalo, Deriving Semantics-Aware Fuzzers from Web API Schemas (Schemathesis)
records.study_design: Comparative evaluation of schema-derived fuzzers against 16 real-world web services
records.population: 16 open-source and production web services with OpenAPI or GraphQL schemas
records.finding: A machine-readable schema is not only documentation but an executable test oracle: schema-derived property-based fuzzing found 1.4 to 4.5 times more unique defects than the next-best fuzzer per target, and was the only tool to find defects in four of sixteen services.
records.applicability_limits: Preprint rather than a peer-reviewed venue record; 16 services is a small sample and the authors evaluate their own tool. Findings depend on schema fidelity, so an inaccurate or generated-after-the-fact spec yields weak fuzzing.

records.source: Wittern, Cha and Laredo, Generating GraphQL-Wrappers for REST(-like) APIs
records.study_design: Tool construction (OASGraph) plus large-scale evaluation over publicly available OpenAPI documents
records.population: 959 publicly available OpenAPI Specification documents
records.finding: Automated transformation from a REST contract to a GraphQL schema succeeded for 89.5 percent of 959 real specifications but with limitations in many cases, the failures traced to missing or ambiguous information in the specifications themselves. Downstream automation is capped by contract quality, not by tooling.
records.applicability_limits: 2018 corpus of OpenAPI 2/3.0 documents; specification quality and tooling have both moved since, so the exact percentage is stale. The principle that under-specified contracts defeat generation is the durable part.

records.version_or_commit: main branch, 5,929 commits, approx 5.8k stars, as at 2026-08-03
records.finding: When contract-first is adopted, author the contract in a language with reuse and linting rather than hand-writing OpenAPI: package house patterns as libraries so the conforming choice is the easy one, and emit OpenAPI, clients and docs from the single definition.
records.applicability_limits: Adds a compile step and a second language to learn between intent and the emitted spec; the emitted OpenAPI is a build artefact, which complicates any workflow that expects to hand-edit it. Vendor-led despite the MIT licence, with roadmap set by Azure needs.
records.counter_evidence: OpenAPI itself (EV-0023) deliberately declines to prescribe design-first over code-first, and code-first generation from annotated handlers keeps spec and implementation from drifting apart by construction.

records.licence: Apache-2.0 (bundles ASM under BSD and Guava under Apache-2.0)
records.finding: Architecture rules can be expressed as ordinary unit tests over compiled bytecode, so layering, slice independence and cycle bans fail the normal build rather than a separate audit tool. A boundary rule that runs in the test suite is the cheapest form of enforcement because it needs no new CI surface.
records.applicability_limits: JVM bytecode only. Cannot see dynamic dispatch through reflection, string-keyed service locators or configuration-driven wiring, so rules can pass while a runtime boundary is still crossed. Says nothing about which boundaries are correct.
records.counter_evidence: Bytecode-level rules bind to package names, so a rename can silently disable a rule unless the rule set itself is reviewed; frozen-violation baselines let debt accumulate invisibly.
records.review: on-change-of:ArchUnit major version or Java module system adoption

records.finding: Boundary enforcement in a dynamic language works at the import graph, with three named contract shapes that cover most real rules: layers (ordered, higher may import lower), forbidden (this must never reach that) and independence (these siblings must not know each other). Declaring the contract in a config file makes the intended architecture a reviewable artefact rather than folklore.
records.applicability_limits: Python only, and static imports only. Runtime imports, plugin registries, dependency-injection containers and string-based dynamic loading are invisible to it. Contract file must be kept in step with package renames by hand.
records.counter_evidence: Import-graph rules cannot express allowed direction of data flow or call semantics, so a module can import only what it should and still be tightly coupled through a shared mutable object.
records.review: on-change-of:import-linter contract types or Python import machinery

records.finding: The same rule engine that fails a build on a boundary violation can emit the dependency graph as dot, mermaid, json or html, so the enforced architecture and the drawn architecture come from one source. Rule classes worth having by default are: no cycles, no orphans, no production code importing dev or optional dependencies, no reaching into another module's internals.
records.applicability_limits: JavaScript, TypeScript and CoffeeScript module graphs. Detects structural violations only; does not evaluate whether the module decomposition is sound. Large monorepos need explicit include and exclude tuning or run time becomes a problem.
records.counter_evidence: Generated graphs of a large codebase are usually unreadable, so the visualisation claim only pays off when scoped to a folder or a rule violation.

records.version_or_commit: unknown (web overview inspected 2026-08-03; template in use since 2005)
records.licence: unknown (site states open source and free including commercial use; specific licence page not inspected)
records.finding: A durable architecture description answers twelve fixed questions, of which only three are diagrams (building block, runtime, deployment). The other nine carry goals, constraints, scope, solution strategy, crosscutting concepts, decisions, quality requirements, risks and glossary. The decision-relevant lesson is that diagrams are a minority of an architecture record; a pack that ships only diagram guidance leaves most of the record unspecified.
